notes: Main disagreements: (1) granularity: coder A split sentences into more units (list items, sample statements, chart cells, sub-clauses), coder B coded the whole sentence once; I kept A's extra units when they state a distinct rule or a rule-bearing sample, and dropped sub-fragments that restate a kept unit (A28/A29 examples inside one 'educational support' sentence, A22 a benefit clause of the declaration practice, A55 a near-repeat) and B's pure rationale or question fragments (B03, B43) and exact repeats (B42). (2) policy_type on neighbouring types: P01 vs P06 for UGA's default rule (kept P01: it is the university-wide default ban, not a silent-syllabus fallback); P69 vs P39 for 'Turnitin scores not be used as a definitive measure' (kept P69: evidence standard); P92 vs P50 for unsupported detectors (P92); P77 vs P56 for 'policy will control' (P77); P83 vs P41/P91 for the learning-goals questions (P83); P41 vs P42 for the 'foundational knowledge' rationale (P41, no mention of novices); P19 vs P20 for pasting the assignment prompt and using the output unchanged (P19); P01 vs P04 for 'not generally permitted ... select assignments' (P01 for the default, P04 for the per-assignment sentence); P65 vs P10 for ask-supervisor-before-using-unvetted-tools (P65). (3) modality for declarative 'will be treated/reported' sentences: set to must, for chart cells: green appropriate expectations should, green permitted uses may, yellow should-not, red must-not. (4) phase for rule-bearing sample text: course-start for course-level default statements, during-work for assignment conduct. Actor 'all' where the sentence addresses employees or any user. Stance agreed on all three documents, so agree_stance_docs is 1.0. Shares are over matched units.
